title: CharacterBody3D moves in wrong direction with context-aware steering, not reproducible in a minimal project
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.7.stable, 4.5.stable


### System information

Artix Linux Runit (up-to-date), Intel i7-6820HQ, AMD Radeon R9 M360 (radv, Mesa 26.1.3-arch1.2), Vulkan

### Issue description

I've been trying to implement a context-based steering system for dynamic object avoidance, with a circle of 16 vectors at equidistant angles representing possible movement directions. Additionally, I've created arrays of interest levels to represent how desirable a direction is when attempting to get to the entity's navigation agent's next path position; danger levels to represent how close obstacles are; and MeshInstance3Ds that sit at the endpoints of raycasts and change colors depending on their direction's interest level to act as a debugging tool. When a direction has a non-0 danger level, interest is subtracted from that direction and added to the opposite direction to discourage the entity from running into an obstacle. I use the following line to calculate the final direction chosen:

```gdscript
chosen_direction += movement_directions[direction] * interest[direction]
```

The issue I'm having is that every sign but the direction the entity actually moves in points to the interest levels being backwards. The color-changing debug meshes are green in the directions opposite where it's going and red in the directions close to where it's going, when I specifically set it up to give their materials' albedo color a higher r value and lower g value if interest is low, and vice-versa. I was further able to confirm that this wasn't just a matter of my color-changing code doing the opposite of what it was supposed to do by writing using the print_rich function to print the interest levels in their associated color. However, while it's moving towards the red meshes and not the green ones, it is still moving in roughly the right direction, but ignores all attempts at getting it to go around obstacles.

Here's what makes me think this is could be an engine bug and not just a problem with my code: when I made a minimal project to demonstrate these issues, using code that's absolutely identical except for lacking some functions relating to things unrelated to movement, such as taking damage and dynamically editing materials, suddenly it was moving towards the green meshes and away from the red ones, like I would expect. It was also moving in the correct direction, and seemed to be effectively avoiding obstacles as expected. I have absolutely no idea how the same exact algorithms could have produced such different behaviors between the two builds.

### Steps to reproduce

Unfortunately, the only way I've found to reproduce this issue is to implement the systems found in the MRP into my specific game project that I've been working on for years. Hopefully the MRP will still provide some clues as to what's going on.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[context-aware-steering.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29531155/context-aware-steering.zip)
